steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Metamorphosis myths involve humans or gods being transformed into animals, plants, stones or constellations

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Ovid's Metamorphoses is the most important literary source — it collects around 250 transformation myths

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Transformations served multiple purposes: punishment, protection, reward, escape and explanation

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Daphne was transformed into a laurel tree to escape Apollo's pursuit — Apollo then adopted the laurel as his symbol

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What were the different purposes of transformation in Greek and Roman myth? | Q: How does the myth of Arachne illustrate the danger of hubris? | Q: Why was Actaeon's transformation particularly unjust?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Punishment (Arachne for hubris), protection (Daphne from Apollo), escape (Io from Hera's wrath), explanation (why spiders weave), and reward (constellations for heroes). | Arachne challenged Athena to a weaving contest and either matched or surpassed her. This hubris — a mortal rivalling a god — led to her transformation into a spider. | Actaeon accidentally stumbled upon Artemis bathing — he did not intend to see her. Yet he was still transformed into a stag and killed by his own hounds, showing divine power operated regardless of mo

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always identify the TYPE of transformation — punishment, protection, escape, explanation Ovid's Metamorphoses is the key source — reference it specifically when discussing Roman versions Consider whether the transformation was just or unjust — this is a common exam angle Link metamorphosis myths to broader themes: power, identity, hubris, divine caprice The emotional impact (pathos) of transformations is important — how does the reader feel about the victim?
